## Why Tailor Presentations?

-   Similar to my slides, you will probably bore people
-   Academics get taught how to talk to researchers and other academics
    -   Many are terrible at working with stakeholders outside of academia
    -   [Many researchers see journals, conferences, and funding reports as dissemination](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6853327/)

## Implementation & Dissemination

-   Entire field on how researchers can assess/study those implementing interventions/etc. and sharing findings
    -   [Using standardized materials](https://teaching.berkeley.edu/resources/course-evaluations-question-bank) you can evaluate the effectiveness of practitioners implementing something you are interested in
    -   Entire theoretical frameworks around this topic
        -   [RE-AIM website](https://re-aim.org/resources-and-tools/figures-and-tables/)
-   Dissemination on how to share research findings in ways that reach your target audience
    -   There is a lot of literature on this field

## Think About Who Will Come Up To Your Poster

-   Would you explain your project in the same manner to the general public as you would
-   Students?
-   Postdocs?
-   Staff?
-   Faculty?

## Questions You Might Receive

-   Why does this matter?
-   What is the point of this study?
-   Why did you do *this* instead of *that*?
-   Why didn't you have AI do this?
-   Tell me why I should care.
-   These are all questions/comments I have received
    -   Can you respond in a single sentence?

## Dissemination Adapted for Posters

-   Create a dissemination plan to address:
    -   Purpose of disseminating research
    -   Audience
    -   Key message to be shared (takeway for anyone)
    -   Methods for dissemination (materials/activities)
    -   Timing of dissemination
    -   Process of evaluating success of dissemination

## For Academics

-   What is the problem you wanted to address
-   Talk about the background literature
    -   What informed your research idea
-   Transition to your RQs
-   Give me brief overview of methods
-   Takeaways for the findings
    -   This is more a poster design topic
-   Discussion
    -   Flip it around with questions for audience
    -   Next steps and areas for collaboration

## Stakeholders

-   Problem statement
    -   Why did you do your study?
    -   What is the big picture answer to why you did the study
    -   Why does this research matter *past* academia
-   Who is affected
-   What decisions can be made from the findings
-   How are you extending the reach of this study?

## Practitioners

-   Problem being addressed
-   What you did (methods) at a high level
    -   Technical jargon loses interest
-   Takeaways
-   Discussion points
    -   What can they tell clients/staff/managers/stakeholders

## General Public

-   Can you explain the complicated parts of your research/methods in as simple of terms as possible
-   Analogies are your friend
-   Be prepared for comments that may not be directly related to your research
    -   How do you direct that to come back into

## Practice Makes Perfect

-   I know most of you will not practice your presentations
-   Reason for having small group presentations
-   Practice your presentation multiple times before giving it to a group
    -   Transitions can be useful but you need to know where they are in your slides
-   Time yourself on specific sections

## For Presentations Next Week

-   Have slides (to both submit and present)
-   Think about what audiences will show up at your poster
    -   Sell us your research project
-   Have your elevator pitch ready
-   When you finish your presentation, think of weak areas
    -   That is where your questions will come up

## Example Presentations

-   Create a title for your presentation
    -   Keep it under 12-15 words
-   Elevator Pitch
    -   Problem statement (no time for background information)
        -   "This is a problem and it has be examined before; however, there is a gap..."
    -   Your purpose statement/aim(s)/RQs/hypothesis(es)
    -   What you are doing in your study (Methods)
    -   What are you hoping to find?
-   Someone in each group will time each elevator pitch

## Example Presentations

-   Walk audience through your project
-   Present your background information
-   Show how you came to your RQs
-   State what the purpose of your research is

## Example Presentations

-   Cover everything for your methods
    -   Be as thorough as possible
-   If you are unsure about your methods, propose multiple methods
    -   Get feedback on pros and cons

## Example Presentations

-   Audience is responsibe for each asking questions and offering feedback
    -   These will serve as your assignments as feedback
    -   I will configure how to leave comments on the presentation through bcourses
-   The point of this is to help find gaps in each other's research projects
-   If something is not clear, ask for clarification

## Disseminating Your Project

-   I like this [research study on innovative dissemination](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7161944/)
    -   Partially because they give a list of rules and that means less reading for me

## Think About Disseminating Results Beyond the Poster

-   Disseminate to the public
    -   LinkedIn
    -   Website portfolio
    -   Twitter/BlueSky/Mastodon
-   Change how you present methodology and findings

## Rules of Dissemination

1.  Get the Basics Right

-   Define objectives, map audience, frame message

2.  Keep the Right Profile

-   Use social media + personal website to expand on research

3.  Encourage Participation

-   Open source, invite others for collaboration

4.  Open Science for Impact

-   Open access pubs/preprints, publish datasets

5.  Remix Traditional Outputs

-   Blog posts in addition to research papers

## Rules of Dissemination

6.  Go Live

-   Talk about your research in less common areas

7.  Think Visual

-   Use art or multimedia interpretations

8.  Respect Diversity

-   Reach should be inclusive

9.  Find the Right Tools

-   Use tools that will be most effective for disseminating your work

10. Evaluate, Evaluate, Evaluate

-   Assess your dissemination activities
-   What works? Why doesn't something work?
